summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a single-cell range.
description: `nonCellGridRange(value)` is the same test as `!isCellGridRange(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

One row and one column, measured by the bounds rather than by how the range was written: the end indices are exclusive, so a single cell is `endRowIndex - startRowIndex === 1` and the same for the columns. A range with a bound left out is open in that direction and is never a single cell.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a single-cell range; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonCellGridRange({ startRowIndex: 0, endRowIndex: 2, startColumnIndex: 0, endColumnIndex: 1 }); // => true
nonCellGridRange({}); // => true
nonCellGridRange(null); // => true
nonCellGridRange({ startRowIndex: 0, endRowIndex: 1, startColumnIndex: 0, endColumnIndex: 1 }); // => false
```
